name: Jacobi plane-rotation symmetric eigensolver
definition: Initialize V=I and A=A₀. While the off-diagonal Frobenius norm exceeds tolerance, choose p≠q maximizing |A_pq| and orthogonal plane rotation G with (GᵀAG)_pq=0; set A←GᵀAG, V←VG. Return diag(A) and V only after convergence.
variables: A real symmetric matrix; G plane rotation; V accumulated orthogonal transformations
assumptions: Real symmetric input; maximal off-diagonal pivot; stable rotation computation; bounded iterations and finite-precision residual checks.
limitations: Repeated rotations can be costly for large dense matrices; clustered eigenvalues make individual eigenvectors nonunique or sensitive.
failure_conditions: Nonsymmetric matrix or unconverged off-diagonal residual
computation: Compute stable annihilating plane rotation, update symmetric entries and optional eigenvector accumulator.

source.citation: University of Texas at Austin, Advanced Linear Algebra: Foundations to Frontiers, §11.3.2 Jacobi's method for computing the Spectral Decomposition. https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~flame/laff/alaff/chapter11-Jacobi-method-spectral-decomposition.html

application: General symmetric matrix diagonalization for numerical analysis.
required_inputs: Real symmetric matrix, pivot schedule, convergence threshold, iteration bound.
incompatible_methods: Confusing a single QR plane rotation with iterative symmetric diagonalization
mechanism_note: Repeated two-sided orthogonal similarity transforms differ from one-sided Givens QR elimination and the QR eigenvalue iteration.

name: Golub–Kahan bidiagonalization recurrence
definition: Start unit v₁, u₀=0, β₁=0. For j≥1 set w=Av_j−β_j u_(j−1), α_j=||w||₂; stop if α_j vanishes, otherwise u_j=w/α_j. Then z=Aᵀu_j−α_j v_j, β_(j+1)=||z||₂; stop if β_(j+1) vanishes, otherwise v_(j+1)=z/β_(j+1).
variables: A real rectangular matrix; u,v left and right basis vectors; α,β bidiagonal coefficients
assumptions: Real rectangular operator with consistent transpose; unit starting vector; positive normalization factors until termination; finite-precision orthogonality monitored.
limitations: Loss of orthogonality and near-zero norms require safeguards; projected singular values are approximations.
failure_conditions: Unhandled zero norm or incompatible adjoint operator
computation: Alternate products by A and A transpose with coupled short recurrences.

source.citation: Netlib, Templates for the Solution of Algebraic Eigenvalue Problems, Golub-Kahan-Lanczos Bidiagonalization Procedure, equations (112)–(116); beta indices shifted by one in this specification. https://www.netlib.org/utk/people/JackDongarra/etemplates/node198.html

application: General reduced numerical representation of rectangular linear operators.
required_inputs: Linear operator, transpose operator, initial vector, dimension and stopping policy.
incompatible_methods: Treating partial projection as complete singular value decomposition
mechanism_note: Alternating rectangular-operator and transpose Krylov recurrence, related to Lanczos on an augmented symmetric operator; differs computationally from dense two-sided Householder reduction. Not independent scientific evidence.

name: BiCGSTAB nonsymmetric linear-system iteration
definition: Initialize r=b−Ax; stop if converged. Fix r̂=r, p=v=0, ρ_old=α=ω=1. At each step set ρ=r̂ᵀr, β=(ρ/ρ_old)(α/ω), p=r+β(p−ωv), v=Ap, α=ρ/(r̂ᵀv), s=r−αv. If s meets tolerance, set x←x+αp and check true residual; otherwise t=As, ω=(tᵀs)/(tᵀt), x←x+αp+ωs, r←s−ωt, ρ_old←ρ. Check convergence before another step; guard all divisions.
variables: A square matrix; b right side; x solution iterate; r,r̂ residual and shadow; α,β,ρ,ω scalars
assumptions: Real nonsingular square system, identity preconditioner, fixed initial shadow residual, finite quantities, nonzero denominators, bounded iterations and a declared absolute/relative residual criterion.
limitations: Irregular convergence and breakdown possible; residual alone may not imply small forward error.
failure_conditions: Zero or near-zero rho, omega or other required denominator before convergence; stagnation, failed true-residual check or nonfinite iterate
computation: Matrix-vector products, dot products and short recurrences; verify true residual before accepting convergence.

source.citation: Barrett et al., Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems (1993), Netlib BiCGSTAB reverse-communication routine, lines 249–385, specialized to the identity preconditioner. https://netlib.org/templates/double/BiCGSTABREVCOM.f

application: General iterative solution of a nonsymmetric numerical system.
required_inputs: Matrix or operator, right-hand side, initial point, tolerance and iteration bound.
mechanism_note: Short stabilized biconjugate-gradient recurrence differs from Arnoldi-based GMRES and symmetric positive-definite CG; no convergence guarantee for every nonsingular system.
